Five guiding questions—centrality, user expectations, frequency, scope, and whether a menu would suffice—help designers choose the right pattern.

items.title: The Case for Cloning Your Coworkers
items.summary: Every CEO Dan Shipper describes building KateBench, a self-improving AI skill trained on 30,000 historical edits that now performs the editor-in-chief's copyediting at scale—democratizing expertise that was previously a bottleneck. The article details plans to clone UX feedback, operational judgment, and other tacit expertise across the team.

items.title: CADDesigner: Conceptual CAD Model Generation with a General-Purpose Agent
items.summary: Proposes CADDesigner, an agentic system that uses a general-purpose language model to generate conceptual CAD models from natural language descriptions, bridging the gap between early design intent and executable geometry. Demonstrates that agent-based approaches can handle the iterative, multi-step nature of conceptual CAD better than single-pass generation.

items.title: Pointer-CAD v2: Plan-Then-Construct CAD Generation with Dimension-Aware Parametric Precision
items.summary: Introduces a plan-then-construct pipeline for parametric CAD generation that explicitly models dimensional constraints and geometric precision, addressing a key gap in prior text-to-CAD systems. Achieves significantly higher dimensional accuracy on standard benchmarks, moving closer to engineering-grade output.

items.title: GraphBrep: Learning B-Rep in Graph Structure for Efficient CAD Generation
items.summary: Proposes representing B-Rep CAD geometry as graphs rather than sequential tokens, enabling more efficient and topologically valid CAD generation. The graph structure captures the face-edge-vertex relationships that define valid solid models, improving generation validity rates for downstream use in CAD/CAM pipelines.

items.title: Adobe Brings ACR's Powerful Non-Destructive Exposure Tools into Photoshop Itself
items.summary: Adobe's major Photoshop update introduces a Light Adjustment Layer (Camera Raw-style), Firefly-powered masking from text instructions, AI Markup tools for communicating edit requests, and a beta AI-Assisted Editor for natural-language complex edits. The update shifts Photoshop toward a craft-first model where AI handles tool selection, letting designers focus on creative decisions rather than software navigation.

items.title: Speaking Design at Scale
items.summary: Design system pattern names like Overview and PageHeader encode months of team decisions into shared vocabulary; AI agents can read the system repository and retrieve the code, guidance, and examples behind each name instantly. This enables a new model where more contributors — and agents — can express design intent in the system's own language, reducing knowledge transfer overhead and accelerating AI-assisted UI generation.

items.title: The Creativity We Outsource — AI, Creativity and the Lost Value of Doing Things Yourself
items.summary: Generative AI delivers design solutions before there is time to explore the problem, removing the productive detours where creative and craft learning happens — especially for students and junior designers. The author proposes designing for Learning Experience (LX) alongside User Experience, treating friction not as a bug but as the site of skill formation in AI-augmented creative workflows.

items.title: The CBI's Latest AI Report on How Design Businesses Can Bridge AI's Execution Divide
items.summary: The CBI report argues that real AI value in design now comes from integrating AI across end-to-end workflows — concept creation through production — rather than isolated experiments. AI's near-term impact augments human judgment and creativity, but automation is hollowing out entry-level design tasks, creating a talent pipeline risk unless firms redesign junior roles around AI-assisted work.

items.title: Anthropic's New Hardware Standard Lets AI Agents Control the Physical World
items.summary: Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard (MHS) is a model-agnostic specification and standardized driver set letting AI agents directly interface with and operate scientific instruments and manufacturing equipment. The system reduces bespoke software integration from weeks or months down to hours, with immediate implications for AI-driven lab automation, process control, and DfAM workflows.

items.title: PTC Advances Leadership in AI-Driven Design with Launch of Onshape FeatureScript MCP Server
items.summary: PTC released the Onshape FeatureScript MCP Server, enabling engineers to describe desired CAD functionality in natural language and have Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini build, test, debug, and refine custom parametric features in FeatureScript automatically. Unlike session-only AI interactions, the generated features become reusable, shareable design tools that capture and scale engineering knowledge across teams without ongoing AI costs.

items.title: Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence
items.summary: World Labs unveiled Atlas, an omni world model pretrained from scratch to natively operate on text, images, video, and 3D data within a shared spatial context—capable of reconstructing scenes from 2–3 images at 1440p, generating minute-long videos, and simulating spatial environments. For AI+design, Atlas demonstrates that a single unified spatial foundation can power next-generation tools for generative 3D modeling, scene reconstruction, and engineering simulation at commercial quality.

items.title: Backflip AI Launches CAD Copilot That Transforms 3D Scans Into Engineer-Quality, Editable CAD Models
items.summary: Backflip AI launched a second-generation foundation model that converts 3D scans, STLs, and mesh files into fully editable parametric CAD models with proper feature trees—available as an Autodesk Fusion add-in—reducing scan-to-CAD costs from ~,500 per part to ~0 and hours of work to minutes. This matters because it makes complete factory floor digitization economically viable for the first time, collapsing a major barrier between physical-part inventories and AI-native manufacturing workflows.

items.title: How AI-Ready Is Your Design System? Now You Can Measure It.
items.summary: open-design-system-bench is an open benchmark that measures whether AI coding agents use a design system correctly when generating UI, scoring four major systems between 52–63 on an AI-readiness composite with none reaching the "AI-native" tier across 898 graded generations. It matters because it surfaces a concrete, measurable gap between the design systems teams have built and the AI agents now consuming them, creating a path to intentionally closing that gap.

items.title: Workflow Lab: Moving Between Design and Code with Agents
items.summary: Figma documents a practical workflow using its MCP server and Code Connect to give coding agents direct access to a team's components, tokens, and layouts so generated code matches design specs—including catching token drift before review. This is a concrete, reproducible template for design-to-code agent pipelines that preserves design intent without manual handoff.

items.title: The Custodial Era of UX: Cleaning Up After AI
items.summary: Nielsen Norman Group argues AI is pushing UX into a "custodial era" where teams ship features faster than they can evaluate them, creating UX debt that practitioners must triage, simplify, and validate. The piece reframes the UX role—from creator to custodian—and calls for embedding UX principles directly into AI generation workflows to prevent future problems.

items.title: Two Adobe AI Features Worth a Web Designer's Attention
items.summary: Adobe added a conversational AI Assistant across Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Premiere, and Frame.io for multi-step task automation, while Illustrator's new Text to Vector tool generates fully editable SVG paths—a capability no major competing AI tool currently offers. Both features mark a meaningful shift in AI integration within the dominant professional creative suite, directly impacting how designers work with vector and production assets.

items.title: Behind the Build: Generative Plugins and Shaders at Figma
items.summary: Figma introduced generative plugins and shaders to the canvas, letting users design tools on demand with the agent building motion and interactivity into any effect, backed by full Figma MCP server integration for view, change, and export of the generated code. This signals Figma moving from a static design canvas to an AI-native, programmable design environment where teams can extend the tool itself using agents.

items.title: Introducing Solaris: An Interface World Model
items.summary: Runway unveiled Solaris, an Interface World Model that generates real-time interactive web and app interfaces frame by frame as users interact—handling both rendering and interaction jointly without any intermediate code representation. For designers, this opens a path to AI systems that produce functional, interactive prototypes in real time, collapsing the gap between design intent and deployed interface and enabling agents to train in far more dynamic environments.
